{{Short description|Mathematician}}
'''Karel Hrbáček''' (born 1944) is professor emeritus of mathematics at [[City College of New York]].<ref>[http://math.sci.ccny.cuny.edu/person/list Faculty listing] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071024161910/http://math.sci.ccny.cuny.edu/person/list |date=2007-10-24 }}, Mathematics Dept., City College, retrieved 2013-12-24.</ref>  He specializes in [[mathematical logic]], [[set theory]], and [[non-standard analysis]].

== Early life and education ==
Karel studied at [[Charles University]] with [[Petr Vopěnka]], looking at large [[cardinal number]]s. He was awarded the degree RNDr. Before his appointment at City College of New York he was an exchange fellow at [[University of California, Berkeley]] and a research associate at [[Rockefeller University]]. In 1980 he received an award from the [[Mathematical Association of America]] for his article on Non-standard Set Theory.<ref>[http://www.maa.org/programs/maa-awards/writing-awards/nonstandard-set-theory Nonstandard set theory]</ref>

==Selected publications==
* 1999: (with [[Thomas Jech]]) ''Introduction to Set Theory'', Third edition. Monographs and Textbooks in Pure and Applied Mathematics, 220. [[Marcel Dekker]] {{ISBN|0-8247-7915-0}}<ref>{{citation|title=Review of ''Introduction to set theory''|first=Gian-Carlo|last=Rota|authorlink=Gian-Carlo Rota|journal=[[Advances in Mathematics]]|volume=29|issue=3|year=1978|page=397|doi=10.1016/0001-8708(78)90023-3|doi-access=}}</ref><ref>L. Gillman, Review of ''Introduction to set theory'', {{MR|0491188}}.</ref><ref>J. M. Henle (1985), Review of ''Introduction to set theory'', 2nd ed., {{MR|0758796}}.</ref>
* 1992: (with David Ballard) "Standard foundations for nonstandard analysis", [[Journal of Symbolic Logic]]  57(2): 741–748 {{mr|id=1169206}}
* 1979: "Nonstandard set theory", [[American Mathematical Monthly]]  86(8): 659–677 {{mr|id=546178}}
* 1978: "Axiomatic foundations for nonstandard analysis", [[Fundamenta Mathematicae]]  98(1): 1–19 {{mr|id=528351}}
